source.title: A comparative evaluation of convolutional neural networks, training image sizes, and deep learning optimizers for weed detection in alfalfa
source.authors: Jie Yang; M. Bagavathiannan; Yundi Wang; Yong Chen; Jialin Yu

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the full article.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares optimizers on weed-classification performance, a different setting and measure from the claim version’s image-classification and language benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The study compares four optimizers across four CNNs and four datasets. Table 3 reports precision, recall, and F1 separately; rows below record the F1 scores for Adam and SGD, the direct comparison named by V4. Image-size and broadleaf-versus-grass findings do not test a listed version. Other optimizer comparisons in Table 3 are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study compares Adam and SGD on held-out weed-image classification after ImageNet pretraining, providing a new setting for V4. It uses fixed initial hyperparameters rather than a tuning search.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' optimizer conclusion: AdaDelta and SGD performed best for AlexNet and GoogLeNet, AdaDelta for VGGNet, and Adagrad and AdaDelta for ResNet. This does not imply SGD always beats Adam; Table 3 contains architecture- and dataset-dependent reversals.
record.recipe_differences: Compares optimizer performance in agricultural weed-image classification using pretrained CNNs and F1 scores; uses the study's initial optimizer hyperparameters and does not report broad tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: The optimizer ranking depends on network architecture and evaluation dataset; F1 scores also vary across VD, TD, TD 1, and TD 2.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper describes only 30 training epochs; the ResNet optimizer loss curves had not stabilized after 30 iterations. Comparisons use weed-detection F1 scores, which do not directly establish the generalization-gap claim.
record.rows_left_out: Other optimizer pairings in Table 3, all precision and recall values, and the image-size comparisons in Table 2 were omitted to keep the extraction focused on the Adam-versus-SGD comparison for V4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label training.
Width variation beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Learning-rate and schedule tuning searches, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, and language modeling. Equal or better Adam training performance accompanying worse held-out performance is not established.
Batch-size variation and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted F1 values and baselines match Table 3. Paired optimizer rows represent the same comparison, not independent evidence. Table 1 specifies 30 epochs, batch size 2, accumulation 5, base learning rate 0.01 and a common step-down schedule; no tuning search or uncertainty estimates are reported. ResNet's training curves remained unstable at the budget limit, so its optimizer differences do not isolate generalization after convergence. V4 concerns held-out performance and does not require a measured training–test gap. Other optimizer comparisons and precision/recall are explicitly declared omitted in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization were not tested.
Network width and test error across the interpolation threshold were not tested.
No fully connected network was evaluated.

The study tests weed image classification, not the listed image-classification and language benchmarks; it does not compare broad hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching optimizers.
Batch size and training-budget effects were not varied.
Dropout and weight decay were not tested.
Sharpness and other generalization measures were not evaluated.
Memorized examples were not identified or removed.
